A) 让他们看到可能实现的目标。 B) 帮助他们摆脱旧有的范式。 C) 鼓励他们重新思考自己的思维模式。 D) 激励他们拥抱新的机会。

analysis.text: What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? 主干 What should learning leaders do，to arouse learners' passion for change 是目的状语，for change 进一步修饰 passion。结构清晰，无陷阱。 47. What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? A) Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved. B) Help them break free from their old paradigms. questions.stem: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 是 say about + 主体的标准细节题问法，无推断信号。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 主干 What does the passage say，about 引出讨论对象，对象是三项并列名词。无从句、无否 定，无陷阱。 48. What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? A) They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job. B) They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change. C) They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization. D) They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. 讲座、培训项目和工作坊能讲清变革的认知层面，但它们在触及行为层面（而行为层面恰是 重大变革的核心）这件事上几乎无效。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects ↔ They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job. the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative ↔ workers' behaviors on the job 预判「改不了行为」直接对应 generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors，两端的否定强度通过 seldom↔generally not 桥接成立。 B) 无中生有 They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change. 把三者说成「在制造变革刺激上不同于 simulation 的干预」，原文只把它们与 simulation 在「能不能触及行为」上作对照，未把它们也定性为 intervention，更未谈 它们「创造刺激」。 C) 与原文相反 They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization. 称它们 「以改变行为为目标」，与原文「在行为层面 seldom effective」的判定方向相反—— 原文恰是说它们做不到这件事。 D) 张冠李戴 They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts. 让 三者「帮助管理者获得员工发展投入的全部成效」，但原文 managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts 是说在常规工作里 managers 几乎看不到全部成效，且这一判断是关于「常规工作条件」整体，不是三者帮助下的 状况。 是什么使模拟成为最富有成效的学习形式之一? A) 它能够通过加速沉浸式学习体验来节省时间。 B) 它让学习者有可能审视自己的技能、知识和学习过程。 C) 它能够为所有参与者提供实践性的学习体验。 D) 它让学习者有可能在没有任何风险的情况下探索、试验和实践。 49. What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? A) Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience. B) Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process. C) Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience. D) Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.

questions.stem: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? 用「What makes X Y?」结构直问 simulation 之所以 fruitful 的原因，原文给出明确归因。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? make 引导 sb./sth. + 宾补结构，simulation 是宾语，one of the most fruitful forms of learning 是 宾补；fruitful 与原文 productive 同义。无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk- free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning. 在数量无限、零风险的模型里探索、实验并反复运用新知的能力，正是让 simulation 成为 最高效学习方式之一的原因。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience. 把 accelerates time 拎出来当主因，但原文里它只是 simulation 优点的描述之一，不 是 is what makes 强调结构所归的原因。 B) 偷换概念 Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process. 取自 skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted，但原文是 processes （业务流程/作业过程），选项改成了 learning process（学习过程），主体偷换；且原 文是 simulation 来 highlight，不是 learners 来 examine。 C) 以偏概全 Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience. 用 practical learning experience 模糊概括 simulation，未含 risk-free、reflect、 experiment 等核心元素；原文 is what makes 主语处也并未用 practical 来归因。 D) ✓ 正确 The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge ↔ Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk. in unlimited, risk-free models ↔without any risk The ability ↔Its potential D 保留了原文的三动词并列与 risk-free 条件，是唯一同时满足两项核心的选项。 参与者在模拟中应该做什么才能获得最大可能的收益? A) 将这种体验仅仅当作游戏。 B) 将所学内容迅速应用到工作中。 C) 培养深层次的理解。 D) 努力与领导者建立紧密联系。 50. What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? A) Take the experience as a mere game. B) Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs. C) Develop a deep level of understanding. D) Strive to connect closely with their leaders.

questions.stem: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 是问明确做法的标准细节题。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 主干 What should participants do，in a simulation 是地点状语，to reap the greatest benefits possible 是目的不定式，possible 后置修饰 benefits。无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing. 为最大化从模拟中获得的收益，参与者应立刻把从体验中所学应用到工作中，以打通「学」 与「做」之间的桥梁。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 Take the experience as a mere game. 让参与者「把体验当作单纯的游戏」，但 If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job 明确把「视为游戏」当作负面后果。 B) ✓ 正确 participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience ↔ Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs. to forge a smooth link between learning and doing ↔to their jobs B 在副词（promptly ↔ immediately）、核心动作（apply what they learn ↔ apply the learning）与落点（to their jobs ↔ between learning and doing）三处与定位句 完全对位。 C) 答非所问 Develop a deep level of understanding. 取自 enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding，那是 simulation 的功效（果），不是参与 者「应当做什么以最大化收益」（因）。 D) 无中生有 Strive to connect closely with their leaders. 让参与者「努力与领导紧密联系」，但全 文从未要求 participants 去与 leaders 建立紧密联系，原文 forge a link 的对象是 learning 与 doing，不是 participants 与 leaders。

questions.stem: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\? 问「文 章说……是什么」，要的是原文给出的具体表述，不是要考生推断。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干是 What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\?，what 是 say 的宾语，is 引导的从句作 say 的真正宾语；不要把 is 误读成主句 谓语。结构清晰、无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. 无限增长不可持续，经济思潮正转向「我们应当在经济模型中以可持续为目标」这一理念。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 we should aim for sustainability in our economic models ↔It should be made sustainable 预判「应追求可持续」与 It should be made sustainable 字面同向，无需推断，直接 锁定。 B) 偷换概念 原文说「可持续经济」对未来重要 a sustainable economy is vital to our future，主 语是「sustainable economy」，而非 It（指 economic growth）本身。 C) 与原文相反 原文明确 GDP growth … should not be the primary goal of governments，作者主 张增长不应是政府首要关切，It should be governments' chief concern 正好相反。 D) 与原文相反 原文首句即否定 GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing，It is an indicator of government performance 正是这个被否定的旧 观点。 51. What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth? A) It should be made sustainable. B) It is vital to the future of humanity. C) It should be governments' chief concern. D) It is an indicator of government performance. 为什么有些人反对政府应当关注幸福的观点? A) 政府无法将幸福强加给公民。 B) 人们的幸福建立在自己的努力之上。 C) 幸福对不同的人意味着不同的事物。 D) 幸福依赖于可持续的经济增长。

questions.stem: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness\? 问「反对的原因」，原文必有一段集中陈述反对理由。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 Why are some people opposed to the idea，后接 that 引导的同位语从句解释 idea 的内容；opposed to 是固定搭配「反对」，不要看成被动语态。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things. 即使把「幸福」理解到最宽泛的程度——视为「繁荣」或「生活满意度」——人们想要的东 西也各不相同。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens 是作者本人的让步 （governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens），而非反对者的反对原 因，时空错位。 B) 无中生有 原文 P2 从未提到「幸福建立在个人努力上」；endeavor 在全文不存在，是凭空添加的 因果。 C) ✓ 正确 people want different things ↔Happiness means different things to different people Don't different people experience different levels of happiness\? ↔ Happiness means different things to different people 「幸福因人而异」与 Happiness means different things to different people 同义， 三个反问句的共同指向皆收束于此。 D) 强加因果 P1 把 sustainable 与 happiness 视为两条不同线索，原文从未说 Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth；该选项把两个概念强行嫁接。 52. Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness? A) Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens. B) People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor. C) Happiness means different things to different people. D) Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth. 哲学家Julian Baggini在最近发表的一篇文章中建议政府做什么? A) 努力减少贫富之间的不平等。 B) 为人们提供获得更好生活的资源渠道。 C) 改变人们的行为以更好地利用社会财富。 D) 利用先进技术改善人们的生活。

options.text: Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens.

options.label: B
options.text: People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor.

options.label: C

questions.stem: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do in a recently published article?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do 是经典「某人的具体 主张」型细节题。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do，suggest 后接 省略 that 的宾语从句 governments do (what)，what 是 do 的宾语前置——理解为 「Baggini 建议政府做什么」。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. 「使用权」是关键：人们不必拥有，而是要能用上那些让他们生活得更好的东西。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 以偏概全 could help reduce inequality 只是 Baggini 主张的「附带效益」（could help），不 是其建议政府该做的核心；选项 A 把附带效益当成主张主体。 B) ✓ 正确 access things that enable them to live well ↔ Provide people with access to resources for a better life 预判「让公民能用上让生活更好的资源」与 Provide people with access to resources for a better life 字面同向。 C) 偷换概念 原文说 changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets，是「社会行为已发生的变化」让现有资产用得更高效；选项把它改成「政府去 改变人们行为以更好利用社会财富」，主动者与目的都被偷换。 D) 以偏概全 Technological advances 在原文同样只是 access 模型成立的「条件」，不是 Baggini 给政府的建议；选项 D 抓了边缘条件而漏掉主张句。 53. B) Provide people with access to resources for a better life. C) Change people's behaviors to put social wealth to better use. D) Make use of advanced technologies to improve people's lives. 为什么WHO认为有必要诉诸改善心理健康的经济效益来证明其建议的合理性? A) 没有GDP增长就无法执行心理健康项目。 B) 心理干预有助于人们的幸福感。 C) 心理健康不良对国家经济体系有害。 D) 政府仍然将经济发展作为优先事项。

questions.stem: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits 问「WHO 为何 觉得有必要诉诸经济利益」，答案不在 WHO 这句的字面，而要从作者紧接的评论中推断政 府的倾向。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 主干 Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations\?，feel the need to do = 觉 得有必要做，to justify 是目的状语——「为了让其建议显得合理」。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity. 然而，WHO 不得不诉诸「改善心理健康带来的经济收益」来说服政府这一举措的成本合 理，这一点本身就说明了问题：只要政府仍把经济置于首位，他们就只关心公民能否继续创 造产值。 54. Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations? A) Mental health programs cannot be executed without GDP growth. B) Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing. C) Poor mental health is detrimental to a nation's economic system. D) Governments still take economic development as their priority.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 无中生有 原文从未说「无 GDP 增长就执行不了心理健康项目」，仅说「政府要看到经济收益才肯 掏钱」；选项 A 把动机改成了执行前提，凭空捏造。 B) 答非所问 Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing 是事实陈述，原文 improving mental health 也支持这一点，但题干问的是「WHO 为何要诉诸经济收 益」，与「干预有益健康」无关。 C) 偷换概念 原文强调「政府以经济为先」是导致 WHO 必须用经济话术的「原因」；选项 C 反过来 说「心理健康差对经济不利」是 WHO 用经济话术的原因——把工具变成了动机来源。 D) ✓ 正确 As long as the economy is their priority ↔ Governments still take economic development as their priority It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits ↔ Governments still take economic development as their priority 「政府只听经济话术」的根本原因即「政府仍以经济为先」，与 Governments still take economic development as their priority 同义。 作者在文章结尾试图传达什么信息? A) 政府的目标应当以繁荣为导向。 B) 政府的目标应当以人为本。 C) 政府在决策时应当考虑公民的观点。 D) 政府应当将持续生产力设为首要任务。

questions.stem: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\? 问作者结尾 要传达的核心信息，是局部主旨题。

A) I can be a reluctant socialiser. I'm sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off. I get restless a few hours into a hangout. I even once went on a free 10-day silent meditation( 冥想) retreat—not for the meditation, but for the silence.
B) So I can relate to author Anneli Rufus, who wrote in *Party of One: The Loners' Manifesto*: "When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. I loved my room. Being there behind a locked door was a treat. To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis."
C) Unsocial tendencies like these are often far from ideal. Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a 'loneliness epidemic' may be exaggerated). In the UK, the Royal College of General Practitioners says that loneliness has the same risk level for premature death as diabetes. Strong social connections are important for cognitive functioning, motor function and a smoothly running immune system.
D) This is especially clear from cases of extreme social isolation. Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement all show how prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations(幻觉) and other forms of mental instability.
E) But these are severe and involuntary cases of aloneness. For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being.
F) Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured. And there are benefits in learning to love your solitude.
G) One key benefit of solitude is improved creativity. Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity at California's San Jose State University, has defined creativity as thinking or activity with two key elements: originality and usefulness. He has found that personality traits commonly associated with creativity are openness (receptiveness to new thoughts and experiences), self- confidence, and autonomy—which may include "a lack of concern for social norms" and "a preference for being alone". In fact, Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising.
H) One reason for this is that such people are likely to spend sustained time alone working on their craft. Plus, Feist says, many artists "are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they're trying to give expression and meaning to through their art." Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process.

A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect—they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. They also found that unsociability had no correlation with aggression (shyness and avoidance did). This was significant because while previous research had suggested that unsociability might be harmless, Bowker and colleagues' paper showed that it could actually be beneficial. Unsociable people are likely to be "having just enough interaction," Bowker says. "They have a preference for being alone, but they also don't mind being with others."

When another person is present, your brain can't help but pay some attention. This can be a positive distraction. But it's still a distraction.

Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialise once more. And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.

P1 Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.

P2 Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.

P3 To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.

P4 Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.

P5 Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.

P6 An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.

P7 Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare "this is us." If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.

reading-2.raw:
P1 GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.

P2 The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? Don't different people experience different levels of happiness? Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.

P3 Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. A government's obligation lies in creating conditions that promote Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. prosperity. And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.

P4 In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on 'real wealth' for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.

P5 As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by 'happiness' advocates. But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.

P6 For example, it's not clear how a 'real wealth' economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. In Western countries, at least—poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation—educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.

P7 To demand that governments set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.

P8 52. Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness? A) Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens. B) People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor. C) Happiness means different things to different people. D) Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "With the increasing application of AI technology, there is a growing concern that it may negatively impact human creativity." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
writing.model: With the increasing application of AI technology, there is a growing concern that it may negatively impact human creativity. In my view, this worry is well-grounded, for excessive reliance on AI can gradually dull our capacity to think and create independently. The reason is straightforward. Creativity is a muscle that strengthens only through active practice. When we ask AI to generate essays, ideas, or solutions at the click of a button, we skip the very struggle that sparks original thinking. Take my own experience as an example. Last semester, I turned to an AI tool whenever an assignment felt difficult. Although the drafts came quickly, I soon realized that my mind had grown lazy: I could no longer brainstorm freely, and my writing lost its personal voice. Therefore, the concern deserves our serious attention. AI should serve as a helpful assistant rather than a replacement for our own minds. Only by keeping our thinking active can we ensure that technology enriches, rather than erodes, human creativity.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 水资源 + 分布 + 不均衡（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语是「水资源」，谓语核心是「分布……不均衡」。立骨架：China's water resources are unevenly distributed。中国的水资源……分布极不均衡 提为主干，「北缺南丰」作为分布不均衡 的具体说明降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 北缺南丰降级为分词/介词结构 北缺南丰 是对「分布不均衡」的进一步说明，不要照中文用 and 平铺成 the north lacks and the south is rich。可降级成 with 独立结构作伴随状语：with the north short of water and the south abundant in it；自古以来 译为句首时间状语 Since ancient times。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调，陈述客观长期事实，用一般现在时 are distributed；「自古以来」只是强调由来已 久，不必改成完成时。 单复数 water resources 作「水资源」固定用复数；the north / the south 特指中国的南北方，加定冠词 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Since ancient times, China's water resources have been unevenly distributed, with water scarce in the north but abundant in the south. 2. 为了有效解决北方严重缺水问题,中国政府实施了南水北调工程(the South-to-North Water Diversion Project)。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 中国政府 + 实施 + 工程（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 中国政府（the Chinese government），谓语「实施」译 launched / implemented， 宾语是工程。骨架：The Chinese government launched the South-to-North Water Diversion Project。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 为了……降级为不定式目的状语 为了有效解决北方严重缺水问题 降级成 To effectively address the severe water shortage in the north 置于句首作目的状语；专名照抄括号里的官方译名。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「实施了」是已完成的具体动作，结合下文 2002 年开工的历史脉络，本句用一般过去时 launched，属对全篇现在时基调的合理偏离。 用词 「解决问题」避免一律用 solve，address / tackle the problem 更地道；「严重缺水」译 severe water shortage。 专名 工程名照抄原文括号官方译名 the South-to-North Water Diversion Project，首字母大写、不可 自译。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: To effectively address the severe water shortage in the north, the Chinese government launched the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. 3. 这是一项跨区域配置水资源的宏大水利工程。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 这 + 是 + 宏大水利工程（主语策略：原句主语） 典型的 A is B 判断句。主语「这」指代上句的工程，译 It；系动词 is；表语是「宏大水利工程」。 骨架：It is a massive water conservancy project。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 跨区域配置水资源作前后置定语 跨区域配置水资源的 是修饰「工程」的长定语：「跨区域」用形容词 cross-regional 前置，「配 置水资源」用现在分词短语 allocating water resources 后置。译为 a massive cross-regional water conservancy project for allocating water resources，长定语前后分流，不全堆在名 词前。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调，下定义属客观事实，用一般现在时 is。 冠词 首次引入这个工程作为一类事物来定义，用不定冠词 a：a massive project。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It is a massive cross-regional water conservancy project for allocating water resources. 4. 历经数十年的规划与筹备,工程于2002年开工建设,分为东、中、西三条线路,总长4350公里,惠及 人口将超过4亿。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 工程 + 开工建设（主语策略：原句主语） 这是一句多动词的长流水句，但核心主谓只有一个：主语 工程（the project），核心谓语是 于 2002年开工建设（began construction in 2002）。其余「历经……」「分为……」「总长……」 「惠及……」全是围绕工程的附加信息，须降级，不能全提成并列谓语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 四个附加信息分别降级安放 历经数十年的规划与筹备 现在分词短语前置 After decades of planning and preparation；分 为东、中、西三条线路 过去分词作定语 divided into eastern, central and western routes；总 长4350公里→with 独立结构 with a total length of 4,350 kilometers；惠及人口将超过4亿 另 起独立句或定语从句 and is expected to benefit more than 400 million people。四股信息各用 不同从属结构挂上，避免 and 一路平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「2002年开工」是过去明确时点，用一般过去时 began；「惠及人口将超过4亿」含「将」，是预 期，用 is expected to benefit / will benefit，体现一般现在/将来。 语态 「分为三条线路」是工程「被」分，用被动 be divided into/is divided into；本篇用过去分词 divided 作定语承接。 数字与单位 4350 公里写 4,350 kilometers；4 亿写 400 million（不是 4 hundred million，hundred 不加 s）；线路是三条，routes 用复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: After decades of planning and preparation, the project began construction in 2002. Divided into eastern, central and western routes with a total length of 4,350 kilometers, it is expected to benefit more than 400 million people. 5. 自2014年通水以来,工程向北方调水累计已超500亿立方米,为北方地区的人民提供了可靠的水资 源,同时也极大地改善了这一地区的生态环境,促进了经济的可持续健康发展。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 工程 + 调水/提供/改善/促进（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是 工程（the project，可用 it 承接）。这句有多个并列动作：「调水超500亿立方米」 「提供水资源」「改善生态环境」「促进发展」。可让「调水」作主干谓语，后三个「提供/改善/ 促进」处理成并列谓语或分词结果状语。骨架：the project has diverted over 50 billion cubic meters of water。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 自……以来前置 + 后续成果降级 自2014年通水以来→Since the water supply began in 2014 作时间状语前置；为北方地区的人 民提供了可靠的水资源 与主干并列；同时也极大地改善了这一地区的生态环境,促进了经济的可持 续健康发展 用现在分词作结果状语 greatly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development，把后两项成果降级成伴随/结 果，主次分明。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「自2014……以来……累计已超」是从过去延续到现在的累积结果，用现在完成时 has diverted； 后续 provided/providing 与 improving 保持同一时间框架。这是本篇唯一最该用完成时之处，务 必识别「自……以来 + 已/累计」这一信号。 主谓一致 主语 the project 是第三人称单数，完成时助动词用 has（has diverted），不是 have。 数字与单位 500 亿 = 50 billion；「立方米」cubic meters 用复数。
